## Here are the victims of the Washington, DC, plane crash


## A group of figure skaters, their coaches and family members were among the passengers of the flight.
Data Visualization Journalist
**ARLINGTON, Va. —**
As the recovery mission is still underway in the Potomac, some of the victims' identities have been released following the Jan. 29 late evening crash between a commercial airplane and an Army helicopter.
There were 64 people on American Airlines Flight 5342 from Wichita, Kansas, to DCA — including 60 passengers and four crew members. The Blackhawk Army helicopter had three soldiers on board.
None of the 67 people on either aircraft are believed to have survived, officials say.
Below are the names of the victims that we know so far. Click on each square to learn more about those killed.
This article will be updated as new information becomes available.
Here's what else we know so far about the people who were aboard the aircraft.

## **Two flight attendants identified**
Hannah Epstein, the daughter of **Ian Epstein**, provided WPBF, a Hearst Television station in West Palm Beach, Florida, with a photo of her father, who was a flight attendant on American Airlines Flight 5342.
In a post on Facebook, the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, also confirmed Ian Epstein's identity. The union, which represents flight attendants, also said **Danasia Elder**, also a flight attendant, was on the plane.
"Our AFA PSA siblings Ian Epstein and Danasia Elder lost their lives last night on the American Eagle PSA Flight 5342 crash," the union said. "Ian and Danasia were Charlotte-based Flight Attendants who began flying in 2020 and 2024, respectively. This news is still very fresh and we want to respect Ian and Danasia’s family and friends during this time and give them time to let us know how they want to honor and remember them. Our commitment is to do everything in our power to make sure this never happens again. Your support means the world to our AFA Family."
CNN reports that its affiliate, WSOC, spoke to Elder's brother-in-law, who confirmed that she was a flight attendant.
In a statement to WPBF, Hannah Epstein said Ian Epstein "was full of life. He loved being a flight attendant because he truly enjoyed traveling and meeting new people. But his true love was his family. He was a father, a stepfather, a husband and a brother! He will be truly missed."
Hannah Epstein said her family "appreciates the outpouring of love and support we’ve received," but added that "at this time we would ask for privacy as we process and grieve our loss."
Hannah Epstein via WPBF
Flight attendant Ian Epstein was among the 64 people aboard American Airlines Flight 5342, according to his daughter Hannah.
* * *

## **Asra Hussain Raza**
**Asra Hussain Raza**, 26, was one of several victims killed, her father-in-law, Dr. Hashim Raza, told CNN.
A daughter of Indian immigrants, Hussain Raza graduated with honors in 2020 from Indiana University and married her college sweetheart in August 2023, Raza said.
Raza was a Washington, D.C.-based consultant who traveled to Wichita twice a month to work on a turnaround project for a hospital there, her father-in-law said. She would often call him at the end of his late emergency room shifts to make sure he stayed awake on the drive home, he told CNN.
“She went out of her way for everybody,” Hashim Raza said.
* * *

## **Coaches, skaters on plane that crashed midair**
Passengers on the jet included a group of figure skaters and their parents and coaches.
Doug Zeghibe, CEO and executive director of the Skating Club of Boston in Norwood, Massachusetts, said two teenage figure skaters, their mothers and two renowned coaches were among 14 members of the U.S. Figure Skating team who were on the American Airlines plane that crashed into the Potomac River near Washington, D.C., according to Hearst Television station WCVB in Boston.
Skater **Spencer Lane**, 16, of Barrington, Rhode Island, and his mother, **Christine Lane**, 49; skater **Jinna Han**, 13, of Mansfield, Massachusetts, and her mother, **Jin Han**; and coaches **Evgenia Shishkova** and **Vadim Naumov**were aboard the plane, according to Zeghibe.

The group was returning from the National Development Camp, which took place after the U.S. Championships in Wichita, Kansas, and was scheduled to board connecting flights from Reagan to New England on Wednesday night.
Spencer Lane's father called his son a "force of a nature," who decided he wanted to try skating three years ago after seeing Nathan Chen in the Olympics.
"His drive and tenacity ... he trained at the Skating Club of Boston five days a week and attended high school online and just committed himself to it," Douglas Lane said.
He said his wife, Christine Lane, was "a creative powerhouse" who would do anything for her children.

Zeghibe said Spencer Lane, who is from Barrington, Rhode Island, was a "highly-talented kid" who was "rocketing to the top of the sport," and Jinna Han was a "wonderful kid, great athlete, great competitor" who was loved by all. Zeghibe said their mothers were "role-model parents" who were dedicated to their children's sport.
* * *

## Friends on an annual hunting trip
**Michael “Mikey” Stovall**,**Jesse Pitcher**, **Jonathan D. Boyd, Alexander "Alex" Huffman and Charles "Charlie" McDaniel**were returning home from their annual hunting trip to Kansas, according to family members.
Stovall’s mother, Christina Stovall, told WBAL, an HTV station, that everyone loved her son and that he is survived by his wife and 11-year-old son.
She added that this was the group of friends' third year of the annual hunting trip.
"They hunt together. They play together. They fish together. The one guy who was sitting next to him was his best friend in the wedding," Christina Stovall said. "Everybody that knows Mikey, you will never hear not one person that will ever say anything bad about him. He always joking, he laughed and carried on. He always just wants to have fun."
Seven friends were on the hunting trip, she said. Pitcher and Stovall worked together, Pitcher’s father, Jameson Pitcher, told The New York Times. Jesse Pitcher had been looking forward to the trip, his dad said, adding his son had been married for just over a year and was in the process of building a home.
Michael Stovall worked as a steamfitter — a tradesperson who installs and maintains piping systems — his cousin, Shawna Slarb, told the Times.
Steamfitters UA Local 602 shared a statement on Facebook confirming four members of the union were among the victims of the plane crash. No names were released. It’s unclear if they were all on the hunting trip.
WBAL, an HTV station in Baltimore, reports that **Robert Prewitt** of Calvert County, Maryland, was on the plane. He was a husband and father of two daughters. Prewitt was an iron worker who was returning home from a work trip.
* * *

## **Samuel 'Sam" Lilley**
A Southeast Georgia native was killed in the midair collision, according to the Hearst Television station WJCL in Georgia. He was the first officer on the American Airlines flight.
According to the family, **Samuel "Sam" Lilley** was a graduate of Richmond Hill High School and Georgia Southern University. He was engaged to be married in the fall.
Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp also confirmed Lilley's passing via a post on X, where he also confirmed the identity of Ryan O'Hara, who was on the Blackhawk helicopter.
* * *

## **Ryan O'Hara, Blackhawk crew chief**
On Thursday, the Parkview High School Marine Corps Junior ROTC in Lilburn, Georgia, said **Ryan O'Hara** was the crew chief onboard the Blackhawk helicopter, according to reports from Hearst Television station WJCL.
The high school is located in Lilburn, which is in metro Atlanta.
"It is with a heavy heart that we announce the passing of one of our own," read a social media post from the MCJROTC. "Class of 2014, former cadet Ryan O’Hara was the Crew Chief on the Black Hawk involved in last night's crash in DC. Our deepest condolences go out to Gary O’Hara and his entire family."
The post said O'Hara is "fondly remembered as a guy who would fix things around the ROTC gym as well as a vital member of the Rifle Team."
The post states that O'Hara leaves behind a wife and a 1-year-old son.
* * *

## **Andrew Eaves, soldier**
In a Facebook post, Carrie Eaves confirmed that her husband, **Andrew Eaves**, was one of the soldiers on the helicopter, according to Hearst Television station WAPT.
"I am sure by now all of you have heard the news of the tragedy that has occurred in DC. My husband was one of the pilots in the Blackhawk," Carrie Eaves said in a Facebook post. "We ask that you pray for our family and friends and for all the other families that are suffering today. We ask for peace while we grieve."
* * *

## Rebecca Lobach, soldier
On Saturday, the Army released the name of the third soldier who died in the collision, which had been withheld for a day at the request of her family.
**Capt. Rebecca M. Lobach**, of Durham, North Carolina, had served as an Army aviation officer since July 2019 and earned an Army commendation medal and an achievement medal. Lobach was a distinguished military graduate in ROTC at the University of North Carolina and ranked in the top 20% of cadets nationwide, according to her family in a statement released by the Army.
"We are devastated by the loss of our beloved Rebecca. She was a bright star in all our lives. She was kind, generous, brilliant, funny, ambitious and strong. No one dreamed bigger or worked harder to achieve her goals," the statement said. "We request that you please respect our privacy as we grieve this devastating loss."
* * *

## **Capt. Jonathan Campos, airplane pilot**
The pilot of the American Airlines aircraft involved in the deadly collision in Washington, D.C., graduated from a Central Florida university, HTV station WESH in Orlando, Florida, has confirmed.
**Capt. Jonathan Campos** graduated from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University in 2015.
Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University issued the following statement: "Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Captain Jonathan Campos (Aeronautical Science,'15). Our thoughts are with his family and the families and loved ones of all impacted by this tragic accident."
* * *

## Grace Maxwell
A student of Cedarville University, which is located northeast of Cincinnati — in Greene County, Ohio — has been identified by the school as one of the victims of the crash, according to HTV station WLWT in Cincinnati.
In a prepared statement, the university said one of its students, **Grace Maxwell**, was among the victims.
WLWT via Cedarville University
Maxwell was a junior at Cedarville University and was originally from Wichita, Kansas, according to WLWT.
The school said Maxwell was a mechanical engineering major and was gearing up to graduate in 2026. She was returning to campus from her home in Wichita, Kansas.
* * *

## A civil rights attorney and two young legal associates
A Harvard-trained civil rights attorney, **Kiah Duggins**, and two bright young law associates, **Sarah Lee Best** and **Elizabeth Anne Keys**, are also among the victims.
Duggins, an attorney at the Civil Rights Corps in Washington, was returning home from visiting her family in Wichita when she died in the collision, according to KWCH.
“We are coming to terms with the grief associated with the loss of our beautiful and accomplished firstborn. Please respect our family’s privacy at this time,” her family said in a statement reported by KWCH.
Duggins got her juris doctor from Harvard Law School in 2021 — where she served as president of the Harvard Legal Aid Bureau — and was set to become a professor at Howard University School of Law this fall, the university confirmed in a statement.
“As a civil rights lawyer, she dedicated her career to fighting against unconstitutional policing and unjust money bail practices in Tennessee, Texas and Washington, D.C.,” the university said in a statement.
Duggins served as a White House intern during the Obama administration and spent nearly a year in Taiwan on a Fulbright grant teaching English, according to her LinkedIn and information provided by Wichita State University, where she got her bachelor’s degree in economics.
Best and Keys, associates of the law firm Wilkinson Stekloff, were also on the plane Wednesday, the firm confirmed in a statement.
“Liz and Sarah were cherished members of our firm—wonderful attorneys, colleagues, and friends,” the firm said in a statement.
A family member confirmed to WLWT that Keys, 33, was on board the plane that collided with the helicopter.

Keys graduated from Madeira High School in 2010, where her mother said she was valedictorian and graduated from Tufts University in 2014. Keys worked as an attorney in Washington, D.C.

## A civil rights attorney and two young legal associates
“Liz had a sharp wit and appreciated it in others**.**Gatherings were always better when Liz was there; she was filled with light and joy. Liz was a dear friend to so many, offering her best self to them all,” Keys’ mother said in a statement to WLWT.
* * *

## Wendy Jo Shaffer
A mother of two from Charlotte, North Carolina, was among the victims killed on American Airlines Flight 5342 Wednesday night, HTV station WXII has confirmed.
Friends and family describe **Wendy Jo Shaffer** as a loving mother, wife and friend. They say she was a kind, strong woman and a friend to everyone she met.
There has been an outpouring of support for the Shaffer family through social media posts.
A GoFundMe page has been set up to help support her family during this difficult time.
* * *

## Sen. Coons of Delaware confirms the names of more skaters killed in the crash
Youth skaters **Sean Kay** and **Angela Yang**, and their coach**Alexandr “Sasha” Kirsanov**, all from Delaware, died in the crash, Sen. Chris Coons, a Democrat from Delaware, said.
“Sasha Kirsanov, Sean Kay, and Angela Yang went to Wichita to pursue their passion for figure skating,” Coons posted on X Thursday. “It is a tragedy that none of them returned home to our state.”
CNN reports that Kirsanov was a former skating coach for the University of Delaware’s figure skating club. That's according to the university’s president, Dennis Assanis, CNN reports.
CNN reports that Kay's father told KYWthat Sean Kay's mother, **Julia Kay**, was also aboard the plane.
* * *

## Bob and Lori Schrock
Two of the victims of the deadly collision have been identified as **Bob and Lori Schrock**, who were Kansas residents who owned property in Oklahoma.
Michael Simpson, a friend of the couple, said that Bob Schrock became a role model and a big part of his life.
"We had more of a mentor-type relationship — taught me a lot on how to live. And we did that through the decade," said Simpson.
* * *

## Casey Crafton
**Casey Crafton** was among the victims killed on the American Airlines flight, according to the Bob Jones University Alumni Facebook page.
Casey Crafton is survived by his wife, Rachel, and the couple's three young sons.
"Please pray for Rachel, their 3 young sons and the rest of the family as they grieve the loss of Casey," the Facebook post said.
* * *

Jesse Pitcher had been looking forward to the trip, his dad said, adding his son had been married for just over a year and was in the process of building a home.
Michael Stovall worked as a steamfitter — a tradesperson who installs and maintains piping systems — his cousin, Shawna Slarb, told the Times.
Steamfitters UA Local 602 shared a statement on Facebook confirming four members of the union were among the victims of the plane crash. No names were released. It’s unclear if they were all on the hunting trip.
WBAL, an HTV station in Baltimore, reports that **Robert Prewitt** of Calvert County, Maryland, was on the plane. He was a husband and father of two daughters. Prewitt was an iron worker who was returning home from a work trip.
* * *
texts.7:
## **Samuel 'Sam" Lilley**
A Southeast Georgia native was killed in the midair collision, according to the Hearst Television station WJCL in Georgia. He was the first officer on the American Airlines flight.
According to the family, **Samuel "Sam" Lilley** was a graduate of Richmond Hill High School and Georgia Southern University. He was engaged to be married in the fall.
Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp also confirmed Lilley's passing via a post on X, where he also confirmed the identity of Ryan O'Hara, who was on the Blackhawk helicopter.
* * *
texts.8:
## **Ryan O'Hara, Blackhawk crew chief**
On Thursday, the Parkview High School Marine Corps Junior ROTC in Lilburn, Georgia, said **Ryan O'Hara** was the crew chief onboard the Blackhawk helicopter, according to reports from Hearst Television station WJCL.
The high school is located in Lilburn, which is in metro Atlanta.
"It is with a heavy heart that we announce the passing of one of our own," read a social media post from the MCJROTC. "Class of 2014, former cadet Ryan O’Hara was the Crew Chief on the Black Hawk involved in last night's crash in DC. Our deepest condolences go out to Gary O’Hara and his entire family."
The post said O'Hara is "fondly remembered as a guy who would fix things around the ROTC gym as well as a vital member of the Rifle Team."
The post states that O'Hara leaves behind a wife and a 1-year-old son.
* * *
texts.9:
## **Andrew Eaves, soldier**
In a Facebook post, Carrie Eaves confirmed that her husband, **Andrew Eaves**, was one of the soldiers on the helicopter, according to Hearst Television station WAPT.
"I am sure by now all of you have heard the news of the tragedy that has occurred in DC. My husband was one of the pilots in the Blackhawk," Carrie Eaves said in a Facebook post. "We ask that you pray for our family and friends and for all the other families that are suffering today. We ask for peace while we grieve."
* * *
texts.10:
## Rebecca Lobach, soldier
On Saturday, the Army released the name of the third soldier who died in the collision, which had been withheld for a day at the request of her family.
**Capt. Rebecca M. Lobach**, of Durham, North Carolina, had served as an Army aviation officer since July 2019 and earned an Army commendation medal and an achievement medal. Lobach was a distinguished military graduate in ROTC at the University of North Carolina and ranked in the top 20% of cadets nationwide, according to her family in a statement released by the Army.
"We are devastated by the loss of our beloved Rebecca. She was a bright star in all our lives. She was kind, generous, brilliant, funny, ambitious and strong. No one dreamed bigger or worked harder to achieve her goals," the statement said. "We request that you please respect our privacy as we grieve this devastating loss."
* * *
texts.11:
## **Capt. Jonathan Campos, airplane pilot**
The pilot of the American Airlines aircraft involved in the deadly collision in Washington, D.C., graduated from a Central Florida university, HTV station WESH in Orlando, Florida, has confirmed.
**Capt. Jonathan Campos** graduated from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University in 2015.
Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University issued the following statement: "Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Captain Jonathan Campos (Aeronautical Science,'15). Our thoughts are with his family and the families and loved ones of all impacted by this tragic accident."
* * *
texts.12:
## Grace Maxwell
A student of Cedarville University, which is located northeast of Cincinnati — in Greene County, Ohio — has been identified by the school as one of the victims of the crash, according to HTV station WLWT in Cincinnati.
In a prepared statement, the university said one of its students, **Grace Maxwell**, was among the victims.
WLWT via Cedarville University
Maxwell was a junior at Cedarville University and was originally from Wichita, Kansas, according to WLWT.
The school said Maxwell was a mechanical engineering major and was gearing up to graduate in 2026. She was returning to campus from her home in Wichita, Kansas.
* * *
texts.13:
## A civil rights attorney and two young legal associates
A Harvard-trained civil rights attorney, **Kiah Duggins**, and two bright young law associates, **Sarah Lee Best** and **Elizabeth Anne Keys**, are also among the victims.
Duggins, an attorney at the Civil Rights Corps in Washington, was returning home from visiting her family in Wichita when she died in the collision, according to KWCH.
“We are coming to terms with the grief associated with the loss of our beautiful and accomplished firstborn. Please respect our family’s privacy at this time,” her family said in a statement reported by KWCH.
Duggins got her juris doctor from Harvard Law School in 2021 — where she served as president of the Harvard Legal Aid Bureau — and was set to become a professor at Howard University School of Law this fall, the university confirmed in a statement.
“As a civil rights lawyer, she dedicated her career to fighting against unconstitutional policing and unjust money bail practices in Tennessee, Texas and Washington, D.C.,” the university said in a statement.
Duggins served as a White House intern during the Obama administration and spent nearly a year in Taiwan on a Fulbright grant teaching English, according to her LinkedIn and information provided by Wichita State University, where she got her bachelor’s degree in economics.
Best and Keys, associates of the law firm Wilkinson Stekloff, were also on the plane Wednesday, the firm confirmed in a statement.
“Liz and Sarah were cherished members of our firm—wonderful attorneys, colleagues, and friends,” the firm said in a statement.
A family member confirmed to WLWT that Keys, 33, was on board the plane that collided with the helicopter.

texts.14:
## A civil rights attorney and two young legal associates
“Liz had a sharp wit and appreciated it in others**.**Gatherings were always better when Liz was there; she was filled with light and joy. Liz was a dear friend to so many, offering her best self to them all,” Keys’ mother said in a statement to WLWT.
* * *
texts.15:
## Wendy Jo Shaffer
A mother of two from Charlotte, North Carolina, was among the victims killed on American Airlines Flight 5342 Wednesday night, HTV station WXII has confirmed.
Friends and family describe **Wendy Jo Shaffer** as a loving mother, wife and friend. They say she was a kind, strong woman and a friend to everyone she met.
There has been an outpouring of support for the Shaffer family through social media posts.
A GoFundMe page has been set up to help support her family during this difficult time.
* * *
texts.16:
## Sen. Coons of Delaware confirms the names of more skaters killed in the crash
Youth skaters **Sean Kay** and **Angela Yang**, and their coach**Alexandr “Sasha” Kirsanov**, all from Delaware, died in the crash, Sen. Chris Coons, a Democrat from Delaware, said.
“Sasha Kirsanov, Sean Kay, and Angela Yang went to Wichita to pursue their passion for figure skating,” Coons posted on X Thursday. “It is a tragedy that none of them returned home to our state.”
CNN reports that Kirsanov was a former skating coach for the University of Delaware’s figure skating club. That's according to the university’s president, Dennis Assanis, CNN reports.
CNN reports that Kay's father told KYWthat Sean Kay's mother, **Julia Kay**, was also aboard the plane.
* * *
texts.17:
## Bob and Lori Schrock
Two of the victims of the deadly collision have been identified as **Bob and Lori Schrock**, who were Kansas residents who owned property in Oklahoma.
Michael Simpson, a friend of the couple, said that Bob Schrock became a role model and a big part of his life.
"We had more of a mentor-type relationship — taught me a lot on how to live. And we did that through the decade," said Simpson.
* * *
texts.18:
## Casey Crafton
**Casey Crafton** was among the victims killed on the American Airlines flight, according to the Bob Jones University Alumni Facebook page.
Casey Crafton is survived by his wife, Rachel, and the couple's three young sons.
"Please pray for Rachel, their 3 young sons and the rest of the family as they grieve the loss of Casey," the Facebook post said.
* * *

## Here are the victims of the Washington, DC, plane crash


## A group of figure skaters, their coaches and family members were among the passengers of the flight.
Data Visualization Journalist
**ARLINGTON, Va. —**
As the recovery mission is still underway in the Potomac, some of the victims' identities have been released following the Jan. 29 late evening crash between a commercial airplane and an Army helicopter.
There were 64 people on American Airlines Flight 5342 from Wichita, Kansas, to DCA — including 60 passengers and four crew members. The Blackhawk Army helicopter had three soldiers on board.
None of the 67 people on either aircraft are believed to have survived, officials say.
Below are the names of the victims that we know so far. Click on each square to learn more about those killed.
This article will be updated as new information becomes available.
Here's what else we know so far about the people who were aboard the aircraft.

## **Two flight attendants identified**
Hannah Epstein, the daughter of **Ian Epstein**, provided WPBF, a Hearst Television station in West Palm Beach, Florida, with a photo of her father, who was a flight attendant on American Airlines Flight 5342.
In a post on Facebook, the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, also confirmed Ian Epstein's identity. The union, which represents flight attendants, also said **Danasia Elder**, also a flight attendant, was on the plane.
"Our AFA PSA siblings Ian Epstein and Danasia Elder lost their lives last night on the American Eagle PSA Flight 5342 crash," the union said. "Ian and Danasia were Charlotte-based Flight Attendants who began flying in 2020 and 2024, respectively. This news is still very fresh and we want to respect Ian and Danasia’s family and friends during this time and give them time to let us know how they want to honor and remember them. Our commitment is to do everything in our power to make sure this never happens again. Your support means the world to our AFA Family."
CNN reports that its affiliate, WSOC, spoke to Elder's brother-in-law, who confirmed that she was a flight attendant.
In a statement to WPBF, Hannah Epstein said Ian Epstein "was full of life. He loved being a flight attendant because he truly enjoyed traveling and meeting new people. But his true love was his family. He was a father, a stepfather, a husband and a brother! He will be truly missed."
Hannah Epstein said her family "appreciates the outpouring of love and support we’ve received," but added that "at this time we would ask for privacy as we process and grieve our loss."
Hannah Epstein via WPBF
Flight attendant Ian Epstein was among the 64 people aboard American Airlines Flight 5342, according to his daughter Hannah.
* * *

## **Asra Hussain Raza**
**Asra Hussain Raza**, 26, was one of several victims killed, her father-in-law, Dr. Hashim Raza, told CNN.
A daughter of Indian immigrants, Hussain Raza graduated with honors in 2020 from Indiana University and married her college sweetheart in August 2023, Raza said.
Raza was a Washington, D.C.-based consultant who traveled to Wichita twice a month to work on a turnaround project for a hospital there, her father-in-law said. She would often call him at the end of his late emergency room shifts to make sure he stayed awake on the drive home, he told CNN.
“She went out of her way for everybody,” Hashim Raza said.
* * *

## **Coaches, skaters on plane that crashed midair**
Passengers on the jet included a group of figure skaters and their parents and coaches.
Doug Zeghibe, CEO and executive director of the Skating Club of Boston in Norwood, Massachusetts, said two teenage figure skaters, their mothers and two renowned coaches were among 14 members of the U.S. Figure Skating team who were on the American Airlines plane that crashed into the Potomac River near Washington, D.C., according to Hearst Television station WCVB in Boston.
Skater **Spencer Lane**, 16, of Barrington, Rhode Island, and his mother, **Christine Lane**, 49; skater **Jinna Han**, 13, of Mansfield, Massachusetts, and her mother, **Jin Han**; and coaches **Evgenia Shishkova** and **Vadim Naumov**were aboard the plane, according to Zeghibe.

## Friends on an annual hunting trip
**Michael “Mikey” Stovall**,**Jesse Pitcher**, **Jonathan D. Boyd, Alexander "Alex" Huffman and Charles "Charlie" McDaniel**were returning home from their annual hunting trip to Kansas, according to family members.
Stovall’s mother, Christina Stovall, told WBAL, an HTV station, that everyone loved her son and that he is survived by his wife and 11-year-old son.
She added that this was the group of friends' third year of the annual hunting trip.
"They hunt together. They play together. They fish together. The one guy who was sitting next to him was his best friend in the wedding," Christina Stovall said. "Everybody that knows Mikey, you will never hear not one person that will ever say anything bad about him. He always joking, he laughed and carried on. He always just wants to have fun."
Seven friends were on the hunting trip, she said. Pitcher and Stovall worked together, Pitcher’s father, Jameson Pitcher, told The New York Times. Jesse Pitcher had been looking forward to the trip, his dad said, adding his son had been married for just over a year and was in the process of building a home.
Michael Stovall worked as a steamfitter — a tradesperson who installs and maintains piping systems — his cousin, Shawna Slarb, told the Times.
Steamfitters UA Local 602 shared a statement on Facebook confirming four members of the union were among the victims of the plane crash. No names were released. It’s unclear if they were all on the hunting trip.
WBAL, an HTV station in Baltimore, reports that **Robert Prewitt** of Calvert County, Maryland, was on the plane. He was a husband and father of two daughters. Prewitt was an iron worker who was returning home from a work trip.
* * *

## **Samuel 'Sam" Lilley**
A Southeast Georgia native was killed in the midair collision, according to the Hearst Television station WJCL in Georgia. He was the first officer on the American Airlines flight.
According to the family, **Samuel "Sam" Lilley** was a graduate of Richmond Hill High School and Georgia Southern University. He was engaged to be married in the fall.
Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp also confirmed Lilley's passing via a post on X, where he also confirmed the identity of Ryan O'Hara, who was on the Blackhawk helicopter.
* * *

## **Ryan O'Hara, Blackhawk crew chief**
On Thursday, the Parkview High School Marine Corps Junior ROTC in Lilburn, Georgia, said **Ryan O'Hara** was the crew chief onboard the Blackhawk helicopter, according to reports from Hearst Television station WJCL.
The high school is located in Lilburn, which is in metro Atlanta.
"It is with a heavy heart that we announce the passing of one of our own," read a social media post from the MCJROTC. "Class of 2014, former cadet Ryan O’Hara was the Crew Chief on the Black Hawk involved in last night's crash in DC. Our deepest condolences go out to Gary O’Hara and his entire family."
The post said O'Hara is "fondly remembered as a guy who would fix things around the ROTC gym as well as a vital member of the Rifle Team."
The post states that O'Hara leaves behind a wife and a 1-year-old son.
* * *

## **Andrew Eaves, soldier**
In a Facebook post, Carrie Eaves confirmed that her husband, **Andrew Eaves**, was one of the soldiers on the helicopter, according to Hearst Television station WAPT.
"I am sure by now all of you have heard the news of the tragedy that has occurred in DC. My husband was one of the pilots in the Blackhawk," Carrie Eaves said in a Facebook post. "We ask that you pray for our family and friends and for all the other families that are suffering today. We ask for peace while we grieve."
* * *

## Rebecca Lobach, soldier
On Saturday, the Army released the name of the third soldier who died in the collision, which had been withheld for a day at the request of her family.
**Capt. Rebecca M. Lobach**, of Durham, North Carolina, had served as an Army aviation officer since July 2019 and earned an Army commendation medal and an achievement medal. Lobach was a distinguished military graduate in ROTC at the University of North Carolina and ranked in the top 20% of cadets nationwide, according to her family in a statement released by the Army.
"We are devastated by the loss of our beloved Rebecca. She was a bright star in all our lives. She was kind, generous, brilliant, funny, ambitious and strong. No one dreamed bigger or worked harder to achieve her goals," the statement said. "We request that you please respect our privacy as we grieve this devastating loss."
* * *

## **Capt. Jonathan Campos, airplane pilot**
The pilot of the American Airlines aircraft involved in the deadly collision in Washington, D.C., graduated from a Central Florida university, HTV station WESH in Orlando, Florida, has confirmed.
**Capt. Jonathan Campos** graduated from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University in 2015.
Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University issued the following statement: "Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Captain Jonathan Campos (Aeronautical Science,'15). Our thoughts are with his family and the families and loved ones of all impacted by this tragic accident."
* * *

## Grace Maxwell
A student of Cedarville University, which is located northeast of Cincinnati — in Greene County, Ohio — has been identified by the school as one of the victims of the crash, according to HTV station WLWT in Cincinnati.
In a prepared statement, the university said one of its students, **Grace Maxwell**, was among the victims.
WLWT via Cedarville University
Maxwell was a junior at Cedarville University and was originally from Wichita, Kansas, according to WLWT.
The school said Maxwell was a mechanical engineering major and was gearing up to graduate in 2026. She was returning to campus from her home in Wichita, Kansas.
* * *

## A civil rights attorney and two young legal associates
A Harvard-trained civil rights attorney, **Kiah Duggins**, and two bright young law associates, **Sarah Lee Best** and **Elizabeth Anne Keys**, are also among the victims.
Duggins, an attorney at the Civil Rights Corps in Washington, was returning home from visiting her family in Wichita when she died in the collision, according to KWCH.
“We are coming to terms with the grief associated with the loss of our beautiful and accomplished firstborn. Please respect our family’s privacy at this time,” her family said in a statement reported by KWCH.
Duggins got her juris doctor from Harvard Law School in 2021 — where she served as president of the Harvard Legal Aid Bureau — and was set to become a professor at Howard University School of Law this fall, the university confirmed in a statement.
“As a civil rights lawyer, she dedicated her career to fighting against unconstitutional policing and unjust money bail practices in Tennessee, Texas and Washington, D.C.,” the university said in a statement.
Duggins served as a White House intern during the Obama administration and spent nearly a year in Taiwan on a Fulbright grant teaching English, according to her LinkedIn and information provided by Wichita State University, where she got her bachelor’s degree in economics.
Best and Keys, associates of the law firm Wilkinson Stekloff, were also on the plane Wednesday, the firm confirmed in a statement.
“Liz and Sarah were cherished members of our firm—wonderful attorneys, colleagues, and friends,” the firm said in a statement.
A family member confirmed to WLWT that Keys, 33, was on board the plane that collided with the helicopter.

## A civil rights attorney and two young legal associates
“Liz had a sharp wit and appreciated it in others**.**Gatherings were always better when Liz was there; she was filled with light and joy. Liz was a dear friend to so many, offering her best self to them all,” Keys’ mother said in a statement to WLWT.
* * *

## Wendy Jo Shaffer
A mother of two from Charlotte, North Carolina, was among the victims killed on American Airlines Flight 5342 Wednesday night, HTV station WXII has confirmed.
Friends and family describe **Wendy Jo Shaffer** as a loving mother, wife and friend. They say she was a kind, strong woman and a friend to everyone she met.
There has been an outpouring of support for the Shaffer family through social media posts.
A GoFundMe page has been set up to help support her family during this difficult time.

## Sen. Coons of Delaware confirms the names of more skaters killed in the crash
Youth skaters **Sean Kay** and **Angela Yang**, and their coach**Alexandr “Sasha” Kirsanov**, all from Delaware, died in the crash, Sen. Chris Coons, a Democrat from Delaware, said.
“Sasha Kirsanov, Sean Kay, and Angela Yang went to Wichita to pursue their passion for figure skating,” Coons posted on X Thursday. “It is a tragedy that none of them returned home to our state.”
CNN reports that Kirsanov was a former skating coach for the University of Delaware’s figure skating club. That's according to the university’s president, Dennis Assanis, CNN reports.
CNN reports that Kay's father told KYWthat Sean Kay's mother, **Julia Kay**, was also aboard the plane.

## Bob and Lori Schrock
Two of the victims of the deadly collision have been identified as **Bob and Lori Schrock**, who were Kansas residents who owned property in Oklahoma.
Michael Simpson, a friend of the couple, said that Bob Schrock became a role model and a big part of his life.
"We had more of a mentor-type relationship — taught me a lot on how to live. And we did that through the decade," said Simpson.

## Casey Crafton
**Casey Crafton** was among the victims killed on the American Airlines flight, according to the Bob Jones University Alumni Facebook page.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This article is a **list of accidents and incidents involving helicopters** and which are notable enough to have an article on Wikipedia. It is grouped by the years in which the accidents and incidents occurred.
1968
*   22 May – Sikorsky S-61L N303Y, operating Los Angeles Airways Flight 841, suffers a mechanical failure in flight which allows the rotor blades to collide with the aircraft's fuselage. It **crashes** at Paramount, California, killing all 23 people on board.  
*   14 August – Sikorsky S-61L N300Y, operating Los Angeles Airways Flight 417, loses a rotor blade in flight and **crashes** at Compton, California. All 21 people on board are killed.
1975
*   17 January – Sikorsky S-55B helicopter **crashes** in Iceland while en route from Reykjavík Airport to Snæfellsnes.
1977
*   10 May – A Sikorsky CH-53 Yas'ur of the Israeli Air Force**crashes** in the Jordan Valley. All 54 people on board are killed.
1978
*   21 June – Two Boeing CH-47 Chinooks of the Imperial Iranian Air Force are **shot down** by the Soviet Air Defence Forces after straying into Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic airspace. One aircraft is destroyed with the loss of eight lives. The other is damaged; it is later repaired with permission from Soviet authorities and returns to Iran.  
*   26 June – Sikorsky S-61 LN-OQS of Helikopter Service loses a rotor blade in flight and **crashes** into the North Sea off Bergen, Norway. All 18 people on board are killed.
1981
*   13 August – Westland Wessex G-ASWI of Bristow Helicopters suffers an engine failure and **ditches** in the North Sea off the coast of Norfolk, United Kingdom. All thirteen people on board are killed.
1982

*   23 July – Bell UH-1 Iroquois N87701 of Western Helicopters is damaged by pyrotechnic explosions and **crashes** while a scene for _Twilight Zone: The Movie_ is being filmed at Indian Dunes, California. Actor Vic Morrow and two child actors are killed on the ground.  
*   14 September – Bell 212 G-BDIL owned by Bristow Helicopters**crashes** while on a nighttime search and rescue mission in the North Sea, killing all six crew members on board.
1983
*   16 July – Sikorsky S-61 G-BEON of British Airways**crashes** into the Atlantic Ocean between the coast of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. Twenty of the 26 people on board are killed.
1984
*   23 October – A Bell UH-1H (number 284) of the Salvadoran Air Force is **bombed** by the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front (FMLN) during the Salvadoran Civil War. All 14 people on board the helicopter are killed, including Lieutenant Colonel Domingo Monterrosa. The bomb was hidden in a reserve radio transmitter used by the FMLN's _Radio Venceremos_ and was captured by Monterrosa's forces as a war trophy.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accidents_and_incidents_involving_helicopters#cite_note-1)
1986

*   18 June – Bell 206 N6TC of Helitech **collides** with Grand Canyon Airlines Flight 6 in mid-air over the Grand Canyon in Arizona, United States. All five people on board are killed, as are all twenty people on board the de Havilland Twin Otter that it collided with.  
*   2 October – A Mil Mi-8 involved in the cleanup effort that followed the Chernobyl disaster**struck the cable of a crane** at Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union, and fell to the ground, killing all four people on board.  
*   6 November – Boeing 234LR Chinook G-BWFC of British International Helicopters suffers a mechanical failure. The aircraft **ditches at sea** off Sumburgh Airport, Shetland Islands, killing 45 of the 47 people on board.
1988
*   13 July – Sikorsky S-61N G-BEID of British International Helicopters suffers an engine fire and **ditches** into the North Sea off the Shetland Islands. All 21 people on board are rescued.
1990
*   27 August – A Bell 206 helicopter carrying musicians and event staff following a concert **crashes** into the side of a ski slope in Elkhorn, Wisconsin, killing all five people on board including blues rock guitarist Stevie Ray Vaughan.
1991
*   4 April – A Bell 412 and Piper Aerostar**collide in mid-air** in a suburb of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. All five people on both aircraft, including United States senator John Heinz, along with two children on the ground, are killed.  
*   25 October – A Bell 206**crashes** into a high-voltage transmission tower near Vallejo, California, during bad weather. All three on board are killed, including Bill Graham.  
*   20 November – A Mil Mi-8 belonging to the Azerbaijani Government is **shot down** by the Armenian military during the Nagorno-Karabakh War and crashes near Karakend. All 22 people on board are killed.
1992

*   28 January – An Azerbaijani Mil Mi-8 is **shot down** near Shusha by Armenian forces. All 44 people on board are killed.
1993
*   26 November – Aérospatiale AS 355 F1 ZK-HIT of the New Zealand Police**collides in mid-air** with Piper Archer ZK-ENX over Auckland. Both aircraft crash, killing all four people on board.
1994
*   2 June – Boeing Chinook HC2 ZD576 of the Royal Air Force**crashes** on the Mull of Kintyre, Argyll. All 29 people on board are killed.
1995
*   19 January – Aérospatiale AS332 Super Puma G-TIGK, operating Bristow Flight 56C is struck by lightning and **ditches** in the North Sea off the coast of Aberdeenshire. All 18 people on board survive.
1996

2003

2006

*   27 December – Eurocopter AS365 Dauphin G-BLUN of CHC Helicopter**crashes** into Morecambe Bay. All six people on board are killed.
2007

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This article is a **list of accidents and incidents involving helicopters** and which are notable enough to have an article on Wikipedia. It is grouped by the years in which the accidents and incidents occurred.
1968
*   22 May – Sikorsky S-61L N303Y, operating Los Angeles Airways Flight 841, suffers a mechanical failure in flight which allows the rotor blades to collide with the aircraft's fuselage. It **crashes** at Paramount, California, killing all 23 people on board.  
*   14 August – Sikorsky S-61L N300Y, operating Los Angeles Airways Flight 417, loses a rotor blade in flight and **crashes** at Compton, California. All 21 people on board are killed.
1975
*   17 January – Sikorsky S-55B helicopter **crashes** in Iceland while en route from Reykjavík Airport to Snæfellsnes.
1977
*   10 May – A Sikorsky CH-53 Yas'ur of the Israeli Air Force**crashes** in the Jordan Valley. All 54 people on board are killed.
1978
*   21 June – Two Boeing CH-47 Chinooks of the Imperial Iranian Air Force are **shot down** by the Soviet Air Defence Forces after straying into Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic airspace. One aircraft is destroyed with the loss of eight lives. The other is damaged; it is later repaired with permission from Soviet authorities and returns to Iran.  
*   26 June – Sikorsky S-61 LN-OQS of Helikopter Service loses a rotor blade in flight and **crashes** into the North Sea off Bergen, Norway. All 18 people on board are killed.
1981
*   13 August – Westland Wessex G-ASWI of Bristow Helicopters suffers an engine failure and **ditches** in the North Sea off the coast of Norfolk, United Kingdom. All thirteen people on board are killed.
1982
texts.1:
*   23 July – Bell UH-1 Iroquois N87701 of Western Helicopters is damaged by pyrotechnic explosions and **crashes** while a scene for _Twilight Zone: The Movie_ is being filmed at Indian Dunes, California. Actor Vic Morrow and two child actors are killed on the ground.  
*   14 September – Bell 212 G-BDIL owned by Bristow Helicopters**crashes** while on a nighttime search and rescue mission in the North Sea, killing all six crew members on board.
1983
*   16 July – Sikorsky S-61 G-BEON of British Airways**crashes** into the Atlantic Ocean between the coast of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. Twenty of the 26 people on board are killed.
1984

All 14 people on board the helicopter are killed, including Lieutenant Colonel Domingo Monterrosa. The bomb was hidden in a reserve radio transmitter used by the FMLN's _Radio Venceremos_ and was captured by Monterrosa's forces as a war trophy.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accidents_and_incidents_involving_helicopters#cite_note-1)
1986

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This article is a **list of accidents and incidents involving helicopters** and which are notable enough to have an article on Wikipedia. It is grouped by the years in which the accidents and incidents occurred.
1968
*   22 May – Sikorsky S-61L N303Y, operating Los Angeles Airways Flight 841, suffers a mechanical failure in flight which allows the rotor blades to collide with the aircraft's fuselage. It **crashes** at Paramount, California, killing all 23 people on board.  
*   14 August – Sikorsky S-61L N300Y, operating Los Angeles Airways Flight 417, loses a rotor blade in flight and **crashes** at Compton, California. All 21 people on board are killed.
1975
*   17 January – Sikorsky S-55B helicopter **crashes** in Iceland while en route from Reykjavík Airport to Snæfellsnes.
1977
*   10 May – A Sikorsky CH-53 Yas'ur of the Israeli Air Force**crashes** in the Jordan Valley. All 54 people on board are killed.
1978
*   21 June – Two Boeing CH-47 Chinooks of the Imperial Iranian Air Force are **shot down** by the Soviet Air Defence Forces after straying into Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic airspace. One aircraft is destroyed with the loss of eight lives. The other is damaged; it is later repaired with permission from Soviet authorities and returns to Iran.  
*   26 June – Sikorsky S-61 LN-OQS of Helikopter Service loses a rotor blade in flight and **crashes** into the North Sea off Bergen, Norway. All 18 people on board are killed.
1981
*   13 August – Westland Wessex G-ASWI of Bristow Helicopters suffers an engine failure and **ditches** in the North Sea off the coast of Norfolk, United Kingdom. All thirteen people on board are killed.
1982

*   23 July – Bell UH-1 Iroquois N87701 of Western Helicopters is damaged by pyrotechnic explosions and **crashes** while a scene for _Twilight Zone: The Movie_ is being filmed at Indian Dunes, California. Actor Vic Morrow and two child actors are killed on the ground.  
*   14 September – Bell 212 G-BDIL owned by Bristow Helicopters**crashes** while on a nighttime search and rescue mission in the North Sea, killing all six crew members on board.
1983
*   16 July – Sikorsky S-61 G-BEON of British Airways**crashes** into the Atlantic Ocean between the coast of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. Twenty of the 26 people on board are killed.
1984
*   23 October – A Bell UH-1H (number 284) of the Salvadoran Air Force is **bombed** by the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front (FMLN) during the Salvadoran Civil War. All 14 people on board the helicopter are killed, including Lieutenant Colonel Domingo Monterrosa. The bomb was hidden in a reserve radio transmitter used by the FMLN's _Radio Venceremos_ and was captured by Monterrosa's forces as a war trophy.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accidents_and_incidents_involving_helicopters#cite_note-1)
1986

*   18 June – Bell 206 N6TC of Helitech **collides** with Grand Canyon Airlines Flight 6 in mid-air over the Grand Canyon in Arizona, United States. All five people on board are killed, as are all twenty people on board the de Havilland Twin Otter that it collided with.  
*   2 October – A Mil Mi-8 involved in the cleanup effort that followed the Chernobyl disaster**struck the cable of a crane** at Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union, and fell to the ground, killing all four people on board.  
*   6 November – Boeing 234LR Chinook G-BWFC of British International Helicopters suffers a mechanical failure. The aircraft **ditches at sea** off Sumburgh Airport, Shetland Islands, killing 45 of the 47 people on board.
1988
*   13 July – Sikorsky S-61N G-BEID of British International Helicopters suffers an engine fire and **ditches** into the North Sea off the Shetland Islands. All 21 people on board are rescued.
1990
*   27 August – A Bell 206 helicopter carrying musicians and event staff following a concert **crashes** into the side of a ski slope in Elkhorn, Wisconsin, killing all five people on board including blues rock guitarist Stevie Ray Vaughan.
1991
*   4 April – A Bell 412 and Piper Aerostar**collide in mid-air** in a suburb of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. All five people on both aircraft, including United States senator John Heinz, along with two children on the ground, are killed.  
*   25 October – A Bell 206**crashes** into a high-voltage transmission tower near Vallejo, California, during bad weather. All three on board are killed, including Bill Graham.  
*   20 November – A Mil Mi-8 belonging to the Azerbaijani Government is **shot down** by the Armenian military during the Nagorno-Karabakh War and crashes near Karakend. All 22 people on board are killed.
1992

*   28 January – An Azerbaijani Mil Mi-8 is **shot down** near Shusha by Armenian forces. All 44 people on board are killed.
1993
*   26 November – Aérospatiale AS 355 F1 ZK-HIT of the New Zealand Police**collides in mid-air** with Piper Archer ZK-ENX over Auckland. Both aircraft crash, killing all four people on board.
1994

On January 26, 2020, a Sikorsky S-76B helicopter crashed into a hillside in the city of Calabasas, California around 25 mi (40 km) northwest of downtown Los Angeles, while en route from John Wayne Airport to Camarillo Airport.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-hr-1) All nine people on board were killed: former professional basketball player Kobe Bryant and his 13-year-old daughter Gianna; baseball coach John Altobelli, his wife Keri and their 14-year-old daughter Alyssa; Sarah Chester and her 13-year-old daughter Payton; basketball coach Christina Mauser and the pilot Ara Zobayan.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-hr-1)

The incident was investigated by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), which concluded that it was caused by continued VFR into IMC: the helicopter entered low cloud cover, which caused the pilot to lose his sense of orientation and thus lose control of the helicopter.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-AAR-21-01_Final_Report-2)
Kobe Bryant (right), former Los Angeles Lakers player, being interviewed by Iván Kasanzew 11 days before the crash

On Sunday, January 26, 2020 at about 9:06 a.m PST (17:06UTC),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) eight passengers and one pilot departed from John Wayne Airport (SNA) in Orange County, California in a 1991 Sikorsky S-76B helicopter, registration N72EX.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-wash-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-BBC51256756-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-KSBY-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-200126-01-7) They were heading to a basketball game at Bryant's Mamba Sports Academy[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-8) in Newbury Park, where he was scheduled to coach his daughter's team.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-WMUR-TV_2020-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ESPN-10) Flight history records showed the helicopter had flown same journey the day before without incident to Camarillo Airport (CMA), a major general aviation airport about 20 minutes by car from Mamba Sports Academy.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-Cohen-11) The previous day's flight had taken only 30 minutes, in contrast,

driving from Bryant's home in Newport Beach to the academy would normally take at least 2 hours.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-Cohen-11)
Several video recordings of the crash site were available and although none showed the crash itself, the sound of the helicopter and the crash was recorded. In particular, surveillance cameras installed at the Agoura Pony Baseball Fields provided overlapping coverage of the final parts of the flight path. The NTSB conducted a visibility study which used frequency analysis to determine when the aircraft made the closest approach to each camera, ground-speed, engine RPM and likely inflight visibility by comparing video recorded during the accident period to clear-sky imagery.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ntsb_vvs-12):1–2 The report concluded that, at the moment of the accident, the estimated visibility ranges were between 1–1.5 miles (1.6–2.4 km).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ntsb_vvs-12):19
The Los Angeles Police Air Support Division had grounded its police helicopters on the morning of January 26 due to poor visibility and low ceiling;[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-liveblog-13) Air Support Division rules require at least 2 miles (3.2 km) of visibility and an 800-foot (240 m)cloud ceiling.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ESPN-Lavigne-200126-14) At the time that N72EX took off from SNA, visibility was 5 miles (8.0 km) with a ceiling of 1,300 feet (400 m). It was operated by Island Express Helicopters, Inc.

as a 14 CFR135 (Part 135) on-demand passenger flight under visual flight rules (VFR).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) Flying through clouds is possible if a pilot elects to operate under instrument flight rules (IFR) but the company's Part 135 operating certificate, issued in 1998, limited operations to on-demand VFR-only flights.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) Even if the company's operating certificate and its own internal policies had allowed for flying under IFR, that option could still have led to lengthy delays and detours (thereby using up any anticipated time savings) because of severe congestion in Los Angeles controlled airspace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LATimes-Mozingo-18) Bryant's celebrity status would not have given the helicopter priority in that airspace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)

According to an automated weather station, the ceiling (distance from ground to bottom of the cloud layer) at the Van Nuys Airport was 1,100 feet (340 m)above ground level. Closer to the site of the crash, the cloud top extended up to 2,400 feet (730 m) above mean sea level.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16)

Audio 3Duration: 3 minutes and 58 seconds.
Audio of the radio transmissions between the helicopter and controllers until contact was lost
In this still frame from a security video, the helicopter can be seen in the upper right (circled in red) flying in the clouds, minutes before the crash happened.
Because visual flight rules prohibit a pilot from flying into or near clouds, the helicopter remained at an altitude of 700 or 800 feet (210 or 240 m) above mean sea level (MSL) while flying northwest from SNA.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) On most of its previous flights to Camarillo, the helicopter had turned west at downtown Los Angeles and flown over the Santa Monica Mountains until it picked up the Ventura Freeway (US 101).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LATimes-Mozingo-18) On January 26, that was not an option for VFR flights because of a deep marine layer which had pushed fog from the Pacific Ocean into the Santa Monica Mountains.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LATimes-Mozingo-18) Instead, the helicopter continued northwest, passed over Boyle Heights near Dodger Stadium and began following the route of the Golden State Freeway (I-5); as the flight approached Glendale,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-21) pilot Zobayan requested permission from the Hollywood Burbank Airportair traffic controllers to transition to following the Ventura Freeway (US 101). Burbank controllers advised him that weather conditions around the airport dictated IFR and held the helicopter circling in a holding pattern for 11 minutes starting at 9:21 a.m.

PST (UTC−08:00)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-Fry-200127-19) before granting it permission to proceed into the controlled airspace around Burbank Airport.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) The hold allowed two inbound flights to land; while holding, Burbank informed Zobayan the cloud top extended to an altitude of 2,400 ft (730 m). Burbank called Van Nuys, which was also operating under IFR, and Van Nuys advised Burbank to take Zobayan north of Van Nuys.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3)

Permission to proceed was granted at 9:32 a.m. (17:32UTC)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) under special VFR, requiring the pilot to stay under 2,500 feet (760 m) altitude.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-CNN-Maxouris-200127-22) The helicopter climbed to an altitude of 1,400 feet (430 m)MSL,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) which Zobayan confirmed with Van Nuys at 9:35 a.m. (17:35UTC).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) After proceeding through Burbank controlled airspace, the flight turned west, following the Ronald Reagan Freeway (SR 118) as it passed into the Van Nuys Airport controlled airspace; the Van Nuys controllers shortly afterward approved a turn southwest towards the Ventura Freeway (US 101) at 9:39 a.m.

(17:39UTC).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-Fry-200127-19) Zobayan then confirmed he was still in VFR flight conditions at 1,500 feet (460 m) and acknowledged the handoff to Southern California air traffic control (SCT).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-WaPo-George-200127-23)

2020 Calabasas helicopter crash  
NTSB investigators examining aircraft debris one day following the crash, January 27, 2020  
Accident  
Date January 26,2020  
Summary Flight into instrument meteorological conditions resulting in spatial disorientation and loss of control  
Site*   Calabasas, California, U.S.
*   34°08′13″N 118°41′32″W / 34.13686°N 118.69231°W  
 [Wikimedia | © OpenStreetMap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#/map/0 "Show in full screen")  
Aircraft
N72EX, the helicopter involved in the accident, pictured in 2018  
Aircraft typeSikorsky S-76B  
Operator Island Express Holdings Inc.  
RegistrationN72EX  
Flight originJohn Wayne Airport, Orange County, California  
DestinationCamarillo Airport, Camarillo, California  
Occupants 9  
Passengers 8  
Crew 1  
Fatalities 9  
Survivors 0
On January 26, 2020, a Sikorsky S-76B helicopter crashed into a hillside in the city of Calabasas, California around 25 mi (40 km) northwest of downtown Los Angeles, while en route from John Wayne Airport to Camarillo Airport.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-hr-1) All nine people on board were killed: former professional basketball player Kobe Bryant and his 13-year-old daughter Gianna; baseball coach John Altobelli, his wife Keri and their 14-year-old daughter Alyssa; Sarah Chester and her 13-year-old daughter Payton; basketball coach Christina Mauser and the pilot Ara Zobayan.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-hr-1)
texts.1:
The incident was investigated by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), which concluded that it was caused by continued VFR into IMC: the helicopter entered low cloud cover, which caused the pilot to lose his sense of orientation and thus lose control of the helicopter.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-AAR-21-01_Final_Report-2)
Kobe Bryant (right), former Los Angeles Lakers player, being interviewed by Iván Kasanzew 11 days before the crash
texts.2: On Sunday, January 26, 2020 at about 9:06 a.m PST (17:06UTC),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) eight passengers and one pilot departed from John Wayne Airport (SNA) in Orange County, California in a 1991 Sikorsky S-76B helicopter, registration N72EX.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-wash-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-BBC51256756-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-KSBY-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-200126-01-7) They were heading to a basketball game at Bryant's Mamba Sports Academy[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-8) in Newbury Park, where he was scheduled to coach his daughter's team.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-WMUR-TV_2020-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ESPN-10) Flight history records showed the helicopter had flown same journey the day before without incident to Camarillo Airport (CMA), a major general aviation airport about 20 minutes by car from Mamba Sports Academy.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-Cohen-11) The previous day's flight had taken only 30 minutes, in contrast,
texts.3:
driving from Bryant's home in Newport Beach to the academy would normally take at least 2 hours.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-Cohen-11)
Several video recordings of the crash site were available and although none showed the crash itself, the sound of the helicopter and the crash was recorded. In particular, surveillance cameras installed at the Agoura Pony Baseball Fields provided overlapping coverage of the final parts of the flight path. The NTSB conducted a visibility study which used frequency analysis to determine when the aircraft made the closest approach to each camera, ground-speed, engine RPM and likely inflight visibility by comparing video recorded during the accident period to clear-sky imagery.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ntsb_vvs-12):1–2 The report concluded that, at the moment of the accident, the estimated visibility ranges were between 1–1.5 miles (1.6–2.4 km).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ntsb_vvs-12):19
The Los Angeles Police Air Support Division had grounded its police helicopters on the morning of January 26 due to poor visibility and low ceiling;[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-liveblog-13) Air Support Division rules require at least 2 miles (3.2 km) of visibility and an 800-foot (240 m)cloud ceiling.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ESPN-Lavigne-200126-14) At the time that N72EX took off from SNA, visibility was 5 miles (8.0 km) with a ceiling of 1,300 feet (400 m). It was operated by Island Express Helicopters, Inc.
texts.4: as a 14 CFR135 (Part 135) on-demand passenger flight under visual flight rules (VFR).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) Flying through clouds is possible if a pilot elects to operate under instrument flight rules (IFR) but the company's Part 135 operating certificate, issued in 1998, limited operations to on-demand VFR-only flights.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) Even if the company's operating certificate and its own internal policies had allowed for flying under IFR, that option could still have led to lengthy delays and detours (thereby using up any anticipated time savings) because of severe congestion in Los Angeles controlled airspace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LATimes-Mozingo-18) Bryant's celebrity status would not have given the helicopter priority in that airspace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)
texts.5:
According to an automated weather station, the ceiling (distance from ground to bottom of the cloud layer) at the Van Nuys Airport was 1,100 feet (340 m)above ground level. Closer to the site of the crash, the cloud top extended up to 2,400 feet (730 m) above mean sea level.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16)

texts.6:
Audio 3Duration: 3 minutes and 58 seconds.
Audio of the radio transmissions between the helicopter and controllers until contact was lost
In this still frame from a security video, the helicopter can be seen in the upper right (circled in red) flying in the clouds, minutes before the crash happened.
Because visual flight rules prohibit a pilot from flying into or near clouds, the helicopter remained at an altitude of 700 or 800 feet (210 or 240 m) above mean sea level (MSL) while flying northwest from SNA.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) On most of its previous flights to Camarillo, the helicopter had turned west at downtown Los Angeles and flown over the Santa Monica Mountains until it picked up the Ventura Freeway (US 101).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LATimes-Mozingo-18) On January 26, that was not an option for VFR flights because of a deep marine layer which had pushed fog from the Pacific Ocean into the Santa Monica Mountains.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LATimes-Mozingo-18) Instead, the helicopter continued northwest, passed over Boyle Heights near Dodger Stadium and began following the route of the Golden State Freeway (I-5); as the flight approached Glendale,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-21) pilot Zobayan requested permission from the Hollywood Burbank Airportair traffic controllers to transition to following the Ventura Freeway (US 101). Burbank controllers advised him that weather conditions around the airport dictated IFR and held the helicopter circling in a holding pattern for 11 minutes starting at 9:21 a.m.
texts.7: PST (UTC−08:00)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-Fry-200127-19) before granting it permission to proceed into the controlled airspace around Burbank Airport.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) The hold allowed two inbound flights to land; while holding, Burbank informed Zobayan the cloud top extended to an altitude of 2,400 ft (730 m). Burbank called Van Nuys, which was also operating under IFR, and Van Nuys advised Burbank to take Zobayan north of Van Nuys.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3)
texts.8: Permission to proceed was granted at 9:32 a.m. (17:32UTC)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) under special VFR, requiring the pilot to stay under 2,500 feet (760 m) altitude.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-CNN-Maxouris-200127-22) The helicopter climbed to an altitude of 1,400 feet (430 m)MSL,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) which Zobayan confirmed with Van Nuys at 9:35 a.m. (17:35UTC).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) After proceeding through Burbank controlled airspace, the flight turned west, following the Ronald Reagan Freeway (SR 118) as it passed into the Van Nuys Airport controlled airspace; the Van Nuys controllers shortly afterward approved a turn southwest towards the Ventura Freeway (US 101) at 9:39 a.m.
texts.9: (17:39UTC).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-Fry-200127-19) Zobayan then confirmed he was still in VFR flight conditions at 1,500 feet (460 m) and acknowledged the handoff to Southern California air traffic control (SCT).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-WaPo-George-200127-23)

On January 26, 2020, a Sikorsky S-76B helicopter crashed into a hillside in the city of Calabasas, California around 25 mi (40 km) northwest of downtown Los Angeles, while en route from John Wayne Airport to Camarillo Airport.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-hr-1) All nine people on board were killed: former professional basketball player Kobe Bryant and his 13-year-old daughter Gianna; baseball coach John Altobelli, his wife Keri and their 14-year-old daughter Alyssa; Sarah Chester and her 13-year-old daughter Payton; basketball coach Christina Mauser and the pilot Ara Zobayan.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-hr-1)

The incident was investigated by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), which concluded that it was caused by continued VFR into IMC: the helicopter entered low cloud cover, which caused the pilot to lose his sense of orientation and thus lose control of the helicopter.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-AAR-21-01_Final_Report-2)
Kobe Bryant (right), former Los Angeles Lakers player, being interviewed by Iván Kasanzew 11 days before the crash

On Sunday, January 26, 2020 at about 9:06 a.m PST (17:06UTC),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ATC-transcript-3) eight passengers and one pilot departed from John Wayne Airport (SNA) in Orange County, California in a 1991 Sikorsky S-76B helicopter, registration N72EX.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-wash-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-BBC51256756-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-KSBY-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LAT-200126-01-7) They were heading to a basketball game at Bryant's Mamba Sports Academy[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-8) in Newbury Park, where he was scheduled to coach his daughter's team.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-WMUR-TV_2020-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ESPN-10) Flight history records showed the helicopter had flown same journey the day before without incident to Camarillo Airport (CMA), a major general aviation airport about 20 minutes by car from Mamba Sports Academy.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-Cohen-11) The previous day's flight had taken only 30 minutes, in contrast,

driving from Bryant's home in Newport Beach to the academy would normally take at least 2 hours.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-Cohen-11)
Several video recordings of the crash site were available and although none showed the crash itself, the sound of the helicopter and the crash was recorded. In particular, surveillance cameras installed at the Agoura Pony Baseball Fields provided overlapping coverage of the final parts of the flight path. The NTSB conducted a visibility study which used frequency analysis to determine when the aircraft made the closest approach to each camera, ground-speed, engine RPM and likely inflight visibility by comparing video recorded during the accident period to clear-sky imagery.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ntsb_vvs-12):1–2 The report concluded that, at the moment of the accident, the estimated visibility ranges were between 1–1.5 miles (1.6–2.4 km).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ntsb_vvs-12):19
The Los Angeles Police Air Support Division had grounded its police helicopters on the morning of January 26 due to poor visibility and low ceiling;[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-liveblog-13) Air Support Division rules require at least 2 miles (3.2 km) of visibility and an 800-foot (240 m)cloud ceiling.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-ESPN-Lavigne-200126-14) At the time that N72EX took off from SNA, visibility was 5 miles (8.0 km) with a ceiling of 1,300 feet (400 m). It was operated by Island Express Helicopters, Inc.

as a 14 CFR135 (Part 135) on-demand passenger flight under visual flight rules (VFR).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) Flying through clouds is possible if a pilot elects to operate under instrument flight rules (IFR) but the company's Part 135 operating certificate, issued in 1998, limited operations to on-demand VFR-only flights.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16) Even if the company's operating certificate and its own internal policies had allowed for flying under IFR, that option could still have led to lengthy delays and detours (thereby using up any anticipated time savings) because of severe congestion in Los Angeles controlled airspace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-LATimes-Mozingo-18) Bryant's celebrity status would not have given the helicopter priority in that airspace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NYMag-Wise-200127-15)

According to an automated weather station, the ceiling (distance from ground to bottom of the cloud layer) at the Van Nuys Airport was 1,100 feet (340 m)above ground level. Closer to the site of the crash, the cloud top extended up to 2,400 feet (730 m) above mean sea level.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Calabasas_helicopter_crash#cite_note-NTSB-update-16)
