On 2 January 2020, a Black Hawk helicopter of the Republic of China Air Force (ROCAF) Air Rescue Group crashed in the Wulai District of New Taipei, Taiwan, while executing a VIP transport mission.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-2) General Shen Yi-ming, Republic of China's Chief of the General Staff (CGS), along with seven other personnel on board, died in the accident.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-CNN0102-3)

The Black Hawk was taking off for a routine mission to visit service personnel in Dong'aoling Radar Station, [Su'ao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su'ao "Su'ao"), Yilan county.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-4) The helicopter lost contact with Songshan Air Base at 8:07 AM, thirteen minutes after taking off and crashed into a mountainside.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-CNN0102-3)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-ASN-1)
General Shen Yi-ming, Chief of the General Staff, was on board the helicopter along with seven other officers and a senior enlisted adviser from the General Staff Headquarters, Ministry of National Defense (MND-GSH), a military correspondent, and three crew members. Shen and seven others including two Major Generals were killed, while five others were injured.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-CNN0102-3)
Eight military servicemembers were killed and 5 were wounded.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-5)

During a news conference on 2 January, General Hsiung Hou-chi, Commanding General of the Air Force, stated that the government had set up a task force to investigate the cause of the accident.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-CNN0102-3) The flight recorders of the aircraft were recovered on 3 January and sent to the Taiwan Transportation Safety Board.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-7) Proprietary hardware within the flight recorders were delivered to Sikorsky Aircraft.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-8)
On 21 July 2020, the Control Yuan announced that Jen I-wei and Chou Shih-kai, both of whom were posted to the Air Force Weather Wing's No. 8 Base at the time of the accident, had been impeached.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-10) It was reported in January 2022 that the Judicial Yuan's Disciplinary Court had barred Jen from working in the public sector for two years. No penalty was issued to Chou, due to insufficient evidence against him.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-11)
President Tsai Ing-wen, along with Generals and Admirals, participated in a moment of silence on the military conference after the helicopter accident
National flag at Dong'aoling Radar Station, scheduled destination of the flight, lowered to half-staff on 4 January in condolence of the accident

This accident occurred nine days before the Taiwanese general election. President Tsai Ing-wen's campaign office and Democratic Progressive Party announced that their presidential and legislative campaign activities would be stopped for three days,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-13) and Han Kuo-yu's presidential campaign office said that Han would cancel campaign events for two days.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-CNN0102-3)
General Mark A. Milley, Chairman of the United States Joint Chiefs of Staff, issued a statement to express condolences to members of the Taiwan military on the death of General Shen and the seven other deceased on behalf of the U.S. military.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-15) The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT), the U.S. representative mission on the island, also issued a statement to extend condolences on the accident, and that it stands ready to assist their Taiwan counterparts in the aftermath.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-16) On 3 January, the flag of the United States at AIT Taipei Main Office flew at half-staff.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-17)

The Japan-Taiwan Exchange Association stated that "they were shocked and grief-stricken at the unfortunate deaths of the eight personnel, including Chief of Staff General Shen Yiming and would be mourned for their valor and service to their nation. At the same time also wishing the five remaining surviving personnel a speedy and healthy recovery."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-:0-18)
Australian Office in Taipei, German Institute Taipei, British Office Taipei, Polish Office in Taipei, along with other foreign missions in Taiwan, as well as Haitian President Jovenel Moïse, Paraguayan Minister of Defense Bernardino Soto Estigarribia and San Christopher and Nevis Minister of Foreign Affairs Mark Brantley and other senior foreign government officials have also expressed their condolences on Facebook or Twitter.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_ROCAF_UH-60M_crash#cite_note-:0-18)

Title: Pilot and nurse killed in medical helicopter crash off Catalina Island identified
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
AVALON, Calif. (KABC) -- The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner has identified the pilot and nurse killed in a helicopter crash off Catalina Island.
The pilot is 59-year-old Steven Robinson. The nurse onboard that medical helicopter was identified as 48-year-old Jessica DeVries.
Tributes are pouring in online for the 48-year-old nurse from Menifee.
"Jessica's family remembers her as a true hero, a devoted mother and an extraordinary woman whose strength, compassion and kindness touched everyone who had the privilege of knowing her. She loved her work and was passionate about helping others during their greatest need," REACH Air Medical Services said in a statement. "Jessica's unwavering spirit will live on in the countless lives she impacted."
"Steve lived a life of service. Over the course of a distinguished aviation career, he served as a United States Marine Corps helicopter pilot, flew Marine One in support of a former United States President, and later continued his service as a medevac pilot with REACH. Every stage of his career was dedicated to serving others with skill, courage, and humility," the statement said. "Steve's family remembers him not only for his remarkable accomplishments, but for the person he was. They describe him as a devoted husband, father, family member and friend who made those around him feel valued, supported and cared for. While his loss is profound, his family is grateful for the example he set and the extraordinary impact he had on so many people."
On Thursday, search and rescue teams located the body of a fifth person that was missing following that helicopter crash, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
Family members identified the missing person as Catalina Romero. They told Eyewitness News that she lived and worked as a housekeeper on Catalina Island for over 20 years and was the mother of three boys.
Relatives and friends said that Romero took her lunch break during her work shift and became ill. They told Eyewitness News that she had an allergic reaction to something she ate and was taken to the emergency room on the island. That's when they decided to send her over to the mainland.
L.A. County Sheriff Robert Luna confirmed at a news conference Thursday afternoon that the missing person was a patient being transported to the mainland for treatment.

"She's my aunt. Right now we're waiting to recover her body and eventually get some closure for the whole entire family right now," said Maria Tamayo. "She was just a loving and caring mother."
A GoFundMe page was set up for Romero to help with her funeral expenses.
Relatives also said Romero's 20-year-old son went with her in the medical helicopter to help translate.

## The crash and aftermath
The aircraft was carrying five people when it went down in the water off of Pebbly Beach around 7:50 p.m. Wednesday soon after takeoff, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. Initial reports indicated that there were only three people on the aircraft.
"We have three people calling for help," a first responder is heard saying in an audio recording of an emergency broadcast. "We do have survivors in the water."
The L.A. County Fire Department later confirmed that two people died, two were hospitalized and a fifth person was missing.
Family identified the missing person in a deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island as a longtime housekeeper who lived on the island.
AIR7 flew over Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center where at least one of the victims was seen being wheeled off a helicopter.

## Top Stories
"Two of those people were last reported (as being) in stable condition, at a higher level of care," Cpt. Stacey Crecy of the U.S. Coast Guard, speaking to reporters at an early morning news conference, said of the survivors.
A memorial service was held Thursday on Catalina Island near the crash site to mourn and pray for those involved in the crash.

## Urgent search and investigation
Search operations continued through the night for the missing person.
Capt. Crecy told reporters at Thursday afternoon's news conference that the search had covered over 130 sq. nautical miles up to that point, with approximately 20 hours of continuous searching for the missing person, and they've had ideal search conditions throughout.
Search and rescue boats were seen on the water early Thursday afternoon. Crecy said teams extended their search.
Hours after the crash, REACH Air Medical Services confirmed that one of their helicopters was involved in the incident.
L.A. County and U.S. Coast Guard officials provide an update on a deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island
"We are aware of an incident involving a REACH Air Medical Services helicopter. At this time, we are gathering information and coordinating with emergency responders and authorities. We are unable to provide additional details at this stage and will share more information when it becomes available. Our immediate concern is for the well-being of those involved.," said a spokesperson for the company.
The L.A. County Fire on-scene lifeguard dive rescue team located the helicopter wreckage under 218 feet of water using a remotely-operated vehicle, L.A. County Fire Chief Anthony Marrone said at Thursday's news conference -- adding that rescue boats arrived within three minutes of them receiving the emergency call.
Sheriff Robert Luna said that sheriff's personnel assisted with the recovery and preservation of debris for federal investigators.
Rescue teams on Thursday continued to search for a missing person after a medical helicopter crashed into the waters near Avalon on Catalina Island.
The National Transportation Safety Board and Federal Aviation Administration are investigating the crash.

## Three people died and two were injured when the REACH Air Medical Services helicopter went down in the water about a mile from Avalon.
### 2 dead, 2 hurt, 1 missing after medical helicopter crash off Catalina Island
The medical helicopter team was airlifting a patient to the mainland who suffered an allergic reaction to food and low oxygen levels. Family members identified the woman as 45-year-old Catalina Hernandez, a mother of three from Avalon. Her body was recovered Thursday in the helicopter wreckage after an extensive search.
Two people were injured in the crash, including Hernandez's son, Alejandro Romero, who was flying with the medical team and his mother. He has several broken bones and was being treated at a hospital, the family said.
REACH identified the other person injured in the crash as flight nurse Brad Sparks, who was taken to UCLA Medical Center and remained under medical care Friday.
"This tragedy has touched every corner of our organization," REACH pacific region president Sean Russell said in a news release. "Steve, Jessica and Brad represent the very best in air medical care—skill, courage, compassion and service to others.”
The company also shared photos of the three crew members in an Instagram post.
Family members described deVries as a true hero and great mother.
"She loved what she did, and we will forever remember her for her strength," her son Gavin said.
The San Bernardino County Fire Department shared images of deVries, highlighting her nearly 20 years of work as a nurse. Authorities said she was dedicated to helping people in emergencies, beginning her career as an emergency medical technician after high school and becoming a registered nurse specializing in difficult responses involving trauma and critical care.
Robinson's aviation career extended beyond his service as a REACH medevac pilot. He had also served as a U.S. Marine Corps helicopter pilot and flew Marine One in support of a former U.S. president, according to REACH.
His family says he was a devoted husband, father, family member and friend. They say they are grateful for the "extraordinary impact he had on so many people."
Oceanside Fire Department Chief Jessamyn Specht said Thursday that the crew had long-standing ties to the department. The helicopter was based at the agency's training center for more than a decade.

AVALON, Calif. (KABC) -- The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner has identified the pilot and nurse killed in a helicopter crash off Catalina Island.
The pilot is 59-year-old Steven Robinson. The nurse onboard that medical helicopter was identified as 48-year-old Jessica DeVries.
Tributes are pouring in online for the 48-year-old nurse from Menifee.
"Jessica's family remembers her as a true hero, a devoted mother and an extraordinary woman whose strength, compassion and kindness touched everyone who had the privilege of knowing her. She loved her work and was passionate about helping others during their greatest need," REACH Air Medical Services said in a statement. "Jessica's unwavering spirit will live on in the countless lives she impacted."
"Steve lived a life of service. Over the course of a distinguished aviation career, he served as a United States Marine Corps helicopter pilot, flew Marine One in support of a former United States President, and later continued his service as a medevac pilot with REACH. Every stage of his career was dedicated to serving others with skill, courage, and humility," the statement said. "Steve's family remembers him not only for his remarkable accomplishments, but for the person he was. They describe him as a devoted husband, father, family member and friend who made those around him feel valued, supported and cared for. While his loss is profound, his family is grateful for the example he set and the extraordinary impact he had on so many people."
On Thursday, search and rescue teams located the body of a fifth person that was missing following that helicopter crash, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
Family members identified the missing person as Catalina Romero. They told Eyewitness News that she lived and worked as a housekeeper on Catalina Island for over 20 years and was the mother of three boys.
Relatives and friends said that Romero took her lunch break during her work shift and became ill. They told Eyewitness News that she had an allergic reaction to something she ate and was taken to the emergency room on the island. That's when they decided to send her over to the mainland.
L.A. County Sheriff Robert Luna confirmed at a news conference Thursday afternoon that the missing person was a patient being transported to the mainland for treatment.
texts.1:
"She's my aunt. Right now we're waiting to recover her body and eventually get some closure for the whole entire family right now," said Maria Tamayo. "She was just a loving and caring mother."
A GoFundMe page was set up for Romero to help with her funeral expenses.
Relatives also said Romero's 20-year-old son went with her in the medical helicopter to help translate.
texts.2:
## The crash and aftermath
The aircraft was carrying five people when it went down in the water off of Pebbly Beach around 7:50 p.m. Wednesday soon after takeoff, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. Initial reports indicated that there were only three people on the aircraft.
"We have three people calling for help," a first responder is heard saying in an audio recording of an emergency broadcast. "We do have survivors in the water."
The L.A. County Fire Department later confirmed that two people died, two were hospitalized and a fifth person was missing.
Family identified the missing person in a deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island as a longtime housekeeper who lived on the island.
AIR7 flew over Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center where at least one of the victims was seen being wheeled off a helicopter.
texts.3:
## Top Stories
"Two of those people were last reported (as being) in stable condition, at a higher level of care," Cpt. Stacey Crecy of the U.S. Coast Guard, speaking to reporters at an early morning news conference, said of the survivors.
A memorial service was held Thursday on Catalina Island near the crash site to mourn and pray for those involved in the crash.
texts.4:
## Urgent search and investigation
Search operations continued through the night for the missing person.
Capt. Crecy told reporters at Thursday afternoon's news conference that the search had covered over 130 sq. nautical miles up to that point, with approximately 20 hours of continuous searching for the missing person, and they've had ideal search conditions throughout.
Search and rescue boats were seen on the water early Thursday afternoon. Crecy said teams extended their search.
Hours after the crash, REACH Air Medical Services confirmed that one of their helicopters was involved in the incident.
L.A. County and U.S. Coast Guard officials provide an update on a deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island
"We are aware of an incident involving a REACH Air Medical Services helicopter. At this time, we are gathering information and coordinating with emergency responders and authorities. We are unable to provide additional details at this stage and will share more information when it becomes available. Our immediate concern is for the well-being of those involved.," said a spokesperson for the company.
The L.A. County Fire on-scene lifeguard dive rescue team located the helicopter wreckage under 218 feet of water using a remotely-operated vehicle, L.A. County Fire Chief Anthony Marrone said at Thursday's news conference -- adding that rescue boats arrived within three minutes of them receiving the emergency call.
Sheriff Robert Luna said that sheriff's personnel assisted with the recovery and preservation of debris for federal investigators.
Rescue teams on Thursday continued to search for a missing person after a medical helicopter crashed into the waters near Avalon on Catalina Island.
The National Transportation Safety Board and Federal Aviation Administration are investigating the crash.

# Identities of pilot and nurse killed in Catalina Island medical chopper crash revealed
## Three people died and two were injured when the REACH Air Medical Services helicopter went down in the water about a mile from Avalon.
### 2 dead, 2 hurt, 1 missing after medical helicopter crash off Catalina Island
The medical helicopter team was airlifting a patient to the mainland who suffered an allergic reaction to food and low oxygen levels. Family members identified the woman as 45-year-old Catalina Hernandez, a mother of three from Avalon. Her body was recovered Thursday in the helicopter wreckage after an extensive search.
Two people were injured in the crash, including Hernandez's son, Alejandro Romero, who was flying with the medical team and his mother. He has several broken bones and was being treated at a hospital, the family said.
REACH identified the other person injured in the crash as flight nurse Brad Sparks, who was taken to UCLA Medical Center and remained under medical care Friday.
"This tragedy has touched every corner of our organization," REACH pacific region president Sean Russell said in a news release. "Steve, Jessica and Brad represent the very best in air medical care—skill, courage, compassion and service to others.”
The company also shared photos of the three crew members in an Instagram post.
Family members described deVries as a true hero and great mother.
"She loved what she did, and we will forever remember her for her strength," her son Gavin said.
The San Bernardino County Fire Department shared images of deVries, highlighting her nearly 20 years of work as a nurse. Authorities said she was dedicated to helping people in emergencies, beginning her career as an emergency medical technician after high school and becoming a registered nurse specializing in difficult responses involving trauma and critical care.
Robinson's aviation career extended beyond his service as a REACH medevac pilot. He had also served as a U.S. Marine Corps helicopter pilot and flew Marine One in support of a former U.S. president, according to REACH.
His family says he was a devoted husband, father, family member and friend. They say they are grateful for the "extraordinary impact he had on so many people."
Oceanside Fire Department Chief Jessamyn Specht said Thursday that the crew had long-standing ties to the department. The helicopter was based at the agency's training center for more than a decade.

Title: Pilot and nurse killed in medical helicopter crash off Catalina Island identified
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
AVALON, Calif. (KABC) -- The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner has identified the pilot and nurse killed in a helicopter crash off Catalina Island.
The pilot is 59-year-old Steven Robinson. The nurse onboard that medical helicopter was identified as 48-year-old Jessica DeVries.
Tributes are pouring in online for the 48-year-old nurse from Menifee.
"Jessica's family remembers her as a true hero, a devoted mother and an extraordinary woman whose strength, compassion and kindness touched everyone who had the privilege of knowing her. She loved her work and was passionate about helping others during their greatest need," REACH Air Medical Services said in a statement. "Jessica's unwavering spirit will live on in the countless lives she impacted."
"Steve lived a life of service. Over the course of a distinguished aviation career, he served as a United States Marine Corps helicopter pilot, flew Marine One in support of a former United States President, and later continued his service as a medevac pilot with REACH. Every stage of his career was dedicated to serving others with skill, courage, and humility," the statement said. "Steve's family remembers him not only for his remarkable accomplishments, but for the person he was. They describe him as a devoted husband, father, family member and friend who made those around him feel valued, supported and cared for. While his loss is profound, his family is grateful for the example he set and the extraordinary impact he had on so many people."
On Thursday, search and rescue teams located the body of a fifth person that was missing following that helicopter crash, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
Family members identified the missing person as Catalina Romero. They told Eyewitness News that she lived and worked as a housekeeper on Catalina Island for over 20 years and was the mother of three boys.
Relatives and friends said that Romero took her lunch break during her work shift and became ill. They told Eyewitness News that she had an allergic reaction to something she ate and was taken to the emergency room on the island. That's when they decided to send her over to the mainland.
L.A. County Sheriff Robert Luna confirmed at a news conference Thursday afternoon that the missing person was a patient being transported to the mainland for treatment.

"She's my aunt. Right now we're waiting to recover her body and eventually get some closure for the whole entire family right now," said Maria Tamayo. "She was just a loving and caring mother."
A GoFundMe page was set up for Romero to help with her funeral expenses.
Relatives also said Romero's 20-year-old son went with her in the medical helicopter to help translate.

## The crash and aftermath
The aircraft was carrying five people when it went down in the water off of Pebbly Beach around 7:50 p.m. Wednesday soon after takeoff, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. Initial reports indicated that there were only three people on the aircraft.
"We have three people calling for help," a first responder is heard saying in an audio recording of an emergency broadcast. "We do have survivors in the water."
The L.A. County Fire Department later confirmed that two people died, two were hospitalized and a fifth person was missing.
Family identified the missing person in a deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island as a longtime housekeeper who lived on the island.
AIR7 flew over Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center where at least one of the victims was seen being wheeled off a helicopter.

## Top Stories
"Two of those people were last reported (as being) in stable condition, at a higher level of care," Cpt. Stacey Crecy of the U.S. Coast Guard, speaking to reporters at an early morning news conference, said of the survivors.
A memorial service was held Thursday on Catalina Island near the crash site to mourn and pray for those involved in the crash.

## Urgent search and investigation
Search operations continued through the night for the missing person.
Capt. Crecy told reporters at Thursday afternoon's news conference that the search had covered over 130 sq. nautical miles up to that point, with approximately 20 hours of continuous searching for the missing person, and they've had ideal search conditions throughout.
Search and rescue boats were seen on the water early Thursday afternoon. Crecy said teams extended their search.
Hours after the crash, REACH Air Medical Services confirmed that one of their helicopters was involved in the incident.
L.A. County and U.S. Coast Guard officials provide an update on a deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island
"We are aware of an incident involving a REACH Air Medical Services helicopter. At this time, we are gathering information and coordinating with emergency responders and authorities. We are unable to provide additional details at this stage and will share more information when it becomes available. Our immediate concern is for the well-being of those involved.," said a spokesperson for the company.
The L.A. County Fire on-scene lifeguard dive rescue team located the helicopter wreckage under 218 feet of water using a remotely-operated vehicle, L.A. County Fire Chief Anthony Marrone said at Thursday's news conference -- adding that rescue boats arrived within three minutes of them receiving the emergency call.
Sheriff Robert Luna said that sheriff's personnel assisted with the recovery and preservation of debris for federal investigators.
Rescue teams on Thursday continued to search for a missing person after a medical helicopter crashed into the waters near Avalon on Catalina Island.
The National Transportation Safety Board and Federal Aviation Administration are investigating the crash.

The medical helicopter team was airlifting a patient to the mainland who suffered an allergic reaction to food and low oxygen levels. Family members identified the woman as 45-year-old Catalina Hernandez, a mother of three from Avalon. Her body was recovered Thursday in the helicopter wreckage after an extensive search.
Two people were injured in the crash, including Hernandez's son, Alejandro Romero, who was flying with the medical team and his mother. He has several broken bones and was being treated at a hospital, the family said.
REACH identified the other person injured in the crash as flight nurse Brad Sparks, who was taken to UCLA Medical Center and remained under medical care Friday.
"This tragedy has touched every corner of our organization," REACH pacific region president Sean Russell said in a news release. "Steve, Jessica and Brad represent the very best in air medical care—skill, courage, compassion and service to others.”
The company also shared photos of the three crew members in an Instagram post.
Family members described deVries as a true hero and great mother.
"She loved what she did, and we will forever remember her for her strength," her son Gavin said.
The San Bernardino County Fire Department shared images of deVries, highlighting her nearly 20 years of work as a nurse. Authorities said she was dedicated to helping people in emergencies, beginning her career as an emergency medical technician after high school and becoming a registered nurse specializing in difficult responses involving trauma and critical care.
Robinson's aviation career extended beyond his service as a REACH medevac pilot. He had also served as a U.S. Marine Corps helicopter pilot and flew Marine One in support of a former U.S. president, according to REACH.
His family says he was a devoted husband, father, family member and friend. They say they are grateful for the "extraordinary impact he had on so many people."
Oceanside Fire Department Chief Jessamyn Specht said Thursday that the crew had long-standing ties to the department. The helicopter was based at the agency's training center for more than a decade.
